crime_highlights: The impact was so severe that Mr. Blackburn’s vehicle was driven across five lanes of traffic and a median before stopping on the grass adjacent to a nearby business.
Tragically, Mr. Blackburn died of his injuries a few hours later.
The out-of-control vehicle was driven by the appellant, Cecil Anthony Boutilier, who had stolen it from a nearby dealership just minutes before.
Upon impact, Mr. Boutilier fled the scene on foot
rationale_highlights: Mr. Boutilier’s very difficult life as an African Nova Scotian - Mi’kmaq man was also properly considered
His mother is Caucasian and his father of Mi’kmaq and African Nova Scotian heritage.
note: Appeal on remand credit only; court says factors properly considered, no stated effect

police found a small baggy, with multiple little packages of what appeared to be cocaine in Mr. Chase’s right rear pocket
rationale_highlights: Mr. Chase has Aboriginal ancestry on his father's side.
She gave proper consideration to the principles of proportionality and parity, together with Mr. Chase’s personal circumstances including his Aboriginal heritage
note: Trial judge gave Gladue reduced weight; appeal court only defers, no clear mitigation

crime_highlights: A significant number of the breaches (conversations) were aimed at undermining the justice system in an effort by the respondent to avoid prosecution of very serious charges.
The respondent’s efforts to get the witness to change her evidence ranged from general discussions to begging, pleading, demanding and threatening.
At one point, the respondent told the young victim, “I should jump through the fucking phone and get you”.
rationale_highlights: The judge took account of the fact that Mr. Cromwell is African-Nova Scotian and that, as a result of systemic racism, there is an overrepresentation of African Canadians behind bars in Canada.

The judge, having assessed the aggravating and mitigating factors, and accepted there is an overrepresentation of African Canadians in custody as a consequence of systemic racism, clearly viewed 18 months as too severe a sentence for Mr. Cromwell.
note: Majority only reports trial view, then raises sentence; dissent says race offset
